data.name: Panfilia
data.gender_notes: Panfilia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'panfilus', meaning 'all-powerful' or 'omnipotent'. In Christian tradition, the name Panfilia is often associated with Saint Pancras, a Roman martyr known for his steadfast faith and devotion. The name Panfilia carries the meaning “All-powerful, omnipotent” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Panfilia usually hope their child will grow to embody all-powerful, omnipotent and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolic of unwavering faith and divine protection.
data.etymology: Panfilia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “All-powerful, omnipotent.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Panfilia total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: פַּנְפִּלְיָה
in_hebrew.meaning: בת האדם, שמה של האישה, נשים שמחות
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם פַּנְפִּלְיָה ממקורות הבבליים והעבריים. הדפיסה 'בת האדם' מציינת את היופי והטבעיות שלה. 'שמה של האישה' עוסק בעוצמה ובעצמאות. 'נשים שמחות' רומז לאופטימיות ולשמחה. השם פַּנְפִּלְיָה נזכר במקרא, בספר שמואל, בסיפורו של דוד ופנילה, האם הכריזמטית. השם עשוי להקנות נשמה של אחוזה והערכה לעצמאות ולעוצמה.

in_greek.name: Πανφιλία
in_greek.meaning: βία της γυναίκας, ομορφιά της γυναίκας, γυναικεία
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο όρος Πανφιλία προέρχεται από την ελληνική γλώσσα. Η μετάφραση 'βία της γυναίκας' υποδηλώνει τη δύναμη και την επιθετικότητα. 'ομορφιά της γυναίκας' αναφέρεται στο φυσιογνωμικό της. 'γυναικεία' υποδηλώνει την ανδρεία και την αυτοπεποίθηση. Ο όρος Πανφιλία δεν αναφέρεται στην Καινή Διαθήκη. Ονομάζεται έτσι επειδή συνδυάζει στοιχεία της ανδρείας και της γυναικείας.

in_latin.name: Panfilius
in_latin.long_meaning: Panfilius proveniente del griego. 'virgo pulchra' se refiere a la belleza de una mujer. 'feminine power' indica la fuerza y la influencia de las mujeres. 'femininity' se refiere a la femineidad. Panfilius no aparece en la Biblia. Se llama así porque equilibra la fuerza de la mujer con su belleza.

in_english.name: Panfilia
in_english.meaning: beautiful woman, feminine power, womanly strength
in_english.long_meaning: The name Panfilia is derived from the Hebrew and Greek languages. 'Beautiful woman' refers to her physical attractiveness. 'Feminine power' indicates her inner strength and resilience. 'Womanly strength' highlights her ability to navigate challenges. Panfilia is not directly mentioned in the Bible but is inspired by the story of David and Peniel, a strong and pious woman. The name is likely to convey a sense of confidence and self-assurance, reflecting the qualities of a strong and pious woman.

historical_references.reference: According to legend, Panfilia was the name of a beautiful princess who was the daughter of King Iasios of Phrygia. She was renowned for her extraordinary beauty and was courted by many suitors. One of them was the god Apollo, who was so smitten by her that he took on human form in order to woo her. However, Panfilia rejected him and chose instead to marry a mortal man named Dionysius. Enraged, Apollo punished Panfilia by sending a plague upon the land. The people prayed to Delphi, where the Pythia revealed that Apollo's anger was caused by Panfilia's rejection of his advances. To appease the god, Panfilia was sent to Delphi to live out her days as a priestess.
historical_references.time_period: Legendary, likely 6th century BCE or earlier

historical_references.reference: Panfilia was a Christian martyr who lived during the late 3rd or early 4th century CE. According to tradition, she was a young girl who was the daughter of a noble family in Phrygia. She was abducted by pagans and forced to participate in their worship of idols. Refusing to comply, she was subjected to various forms of torture and eventually beheaded. She is now venerated as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church and her feast day is celebrated on January 10th.
